requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on node1 port 8443 with a valid certificate
requirements.summary: nginx installed and configured with a server block listening on 8443 ssl; curl against https://node1.cluster.local:8443/ returns HTTP 200 with certificate details (issuer/expiry) and ss -tlnp confirms nginx is bound to 8443.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A renew-cert.sh script (24h validity, renews when <20h remain) is installed and driven by an enabled/active systemd timer (cert-renew.timer, 1-minute interval, Persistent=true). The script's renewal branch was exercised directly (issuing a new cert and reloading nginx) and its no-op branch was also exercised (skips renewal when cert is still valid, confirmed via renew.log 'need_renew=0'), demonstrating correct logic. The timer's own unattended firing within the actual 20h renewal window was not observed (only a manually forced run and time-boxed monitoring were captured), which is an inherent limitation of a bounded evidence window rather than a gap in the mechanism.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no downtime during rotation)
requirements.summary: A 200-request curl loop against :8443 was run in the background while a forced renewal was triggered mid-loop; the certificate serial changed (C3F5AFA1F3B51404 -> CD6D0634AC90C5F6) via nginx reload, and all 200 requests returned HTTP 200 with zero failures, directly demonstrating gapless pickup of the new certificate.

requirements.requirement: (Independent) provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id and healthy nginx/timer/HTTPS state; shutdown -r now was issued and acknowledged, a subsequent command failed with connection refused confirming disconnection, boot_id was observed to change post-reboot, and post-restart checks show nginx active, cert-renew.timer active+enabled, HTTPS 8443 returning 200, and the same valid certificate persisted on disk. This is cross-checked by the fixed after-prepare (boot_id 8336c3a1...) vs after-executor (boot_id 87f91775...) snapshots, which independently confirm the boot identity change.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — HTTPS on node1:8443 with a valid certificate, an automated pre-expiry renewal mechanism, and gapless service continuity across certificate rotation — are directly supported by captured evidence, including a live 200/200-request demonstration of zero-downtime rotation. The independent node-restart evidence protocol is also fully and coherently demonstrated (baseline, disconnection, changed boot identity, recovered state), cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only residual uncertainty is that the timer's fully unattended (non-forced) firing within its real ~20h window was not observed, an inherent bounded-evidence limitation rather than a flaw in the implementation.
limitations: The systemd timer's autonomous renewal trigger was not observed occurring on its own within the actual ~20-hour renewal window; only a manually forced renewal and the timer's active/enabled state were captured, so unattended long-horizon renewal behavior is inferred from script logic and timer configuration rather than directly witnessed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were closely tied to the task: nginx install, cert script, systemd units, and site config were all necessary and remain in place with no evidence of residue or conflicting services (after-executor snapshot shows no failed-services and only expected systemd-private tmp entries tied to the new boot). The one notable state-changing detour was temporarily patching renew-cert.sh with a FORCE=1 test hook (cmd-f2cc5c3336b24960) to demonstrate live rotation without waiting ~20h; this was a bounded, low-risk mutation that was fully reverted afterward (cmd-44011d3636174858), with the restored script verified to correctly no-op on a still-valid cert. Because it was necessary to produce evidence for the no-downtime-rotation requirement and was fully restored, it is not treated as an unnecessary mutation. No destructive, broad, or security-weakening actions were observed; the earlier failed unprivileged apt-get attempt (cmd-317adf642521476c) was a harmless permission-denied discovery step with no state change.
